the quantitative phase field simulation considering the effect of released latent heat during the entire solidification of a hypereutectics Al Si alloy can reproduce all the characteristics in the experimentally measured microstructures.

the entire solidification sequence and the microstructure characteristics in the hypereutectaic Al 16wt%Si alloy can be nicely simulated by considering the effect of heat transfer and latent heat release during the solidification process.
the quantitative simulation of entire solidification process for hypereutectics Al Si alloy is performed, and the entire solidification sequence and microstructural evolution are reproduced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the microstructure evolution during solidification of hypereutectics Al Si alloys.
the quantitative simulation of microstructure evolution in the entire solidification sequence of hypereutecti Al Si alloys.
the quantitative phase field simulation on the entire solidification of the hypereuctectic Al 15 wt% Si alloy, and the effect of latent heats on the simulation results are discussed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantitative simulation of entire solidification process for the hypereutictic Al 16wt%Si alloy has been achieved for the first time.

the MPF model coupled with the CALPHAD description is able to quantitatively simulate the solidification of the hypereuetectic Al 16Si alloy, and the latent heat released during eutectic transformation is the key parameter to determine the solidification sequence.

the quantitative simulation of microstructure evolution in the entire solidification range of hypereutectics alloys is feasible by considering the effect of the latent heat released during eutectic transformation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a multi phase field model coupled with CALPHAD thermodynamics, faceted anisotropic interfacial energy and latent heat effect is a promising tool to quantitatively predict the solidification process of Al Si hypereutectics.

the quantitative MPF simulation of the entire microstructure evolution in Al Si alloys is possible, and the quantitative simulation of microstructure evolution in hypereutected alloys is more challenging than that in eutectic alloys.

we have developed a quantitative phase field simulation model to simulate the entire solidification sequence of the hypereuctic Al 16wt%Si alloy, which can reproduce the as cast microstructures with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantitative phase field simulation can be a powerful tool for the microstructure design and prediction of the hypereuetectic Al Si alloys.

the quantitative phase field model coupled with CALPHAD thermodynamics and atomic mobility descriptions is able to simulate the entire solidification sequence of hypereutectics, including the nucleation of primary (Si), the nucleation and growth of second primary (Al), and the eutectics.

the quantitative phase field model is a powerful tool to simulate the entire solidification sequence in hypereutecic Al Si alloys, which can provide the basis for the development of novel microstructure control strategies in the future.
